title: Vic Dickenson's worn-out horn and the Toronto instrument manufacturer
summary: A friend wrote the Toronto instrument company about Vic Dickenson's old trombone; the manager invited Vic and Autrey, whose Fats Waller-era horn was falling apart, to the factory.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: By the way, they gave me this horn there.
: Oh, really?
Yeah.
: Herman has just taken a trumpet out of the case, showing me. Hey, that's great.
And they gave me that.
: What was the occasion of giving you the horn?

Well, that's an interesting story. I was there with Red, and meantime, Vic Dickenson had an old -- he'd been playing, been using for years, and the darn thing was about gone, you know. And what, 30, what, 30 something years, I think he'd had this.
: Yeah, let me hold the mike here. And then you have two hands for that. I've got it. Okay.
Thank you. And --
: You're talking about Vic and his --
Yeah, so --
-- horn that was falling apart.

-- a friend of ours wrote in to the company, the head of the company and asked them, told them that Vic Dickenson needed a horn, and could they do something about it. So the big manager wrote -- that's it. Let's turn it around. Notice the name of that?
: Right. Uh-huh. This is your European trip, now. In 1968.
Right.
With Red Richards, Vic Dickenson, Herman Autrey, Woodie Powell, Dan Mastry, and George Reed.
Keep that.
Okay.

And that -- so when the man comes in to -- into Toronto he give him a horn. So he -- the manager came in to this club where we were playing, and they asked for Vic, and Vic went down and started with him, said -- he said well, said Herman, come over and join us. I said thank you. And they would talk, and Vic showed them the horn that he had, and the man said that's awful. Wow! Said Herman, what kind of horn do you use? I told him, and he said well I have a [ ]. I said, in fact, Fats Waller gave it to me in 1936.
And he said well let me see it? And he looked at it (laughs). It was just hanging together, you know. Believe me.
(Laughter.)
So he said okay, Vic, come on out to the factory and -- they had a factory there in Toronto -- come out to the factory Monday. And Herman, you come along with him. I said okay.
Now he didn't promise me a horn. He said come on out.
